title: Automatic client-rewrite spec for legacy endpoint removal
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Deliver a product-spec and acceptance criteria for an automated client-rewrite utility and coordinated rollout plan that enables removal of the legacy streaming and buffered endpoints with minimal customer friction. The tool will (a) detect usage patterns in client repos and SDKs, (b) propose deterministic code edits or SDK configuration changes, (c) generate migration patches/patch-PRs and a step-by-step migration report, and (d) provide a gated rollout path (shadow, opt-in, automatic) tied to telemetry and safety checks. Scope excludes server-side binary compatibility shims and on-prem plugin packaging for air-gapped installs; those are tracked in a parallel eng epic.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A public spec document (Confluence) describing rewrite heuristics, fallbacks, and safe rollback semantics is published and reviewed by Eng and DX (link included).

2) CLI utility prototype capable of transforming the 3 most common legacy patterns into unified inference calls (examples: legacy /v0/stream => /v1/chat.stream; legacy buffed generate usage => unified generate with streaming:false) with zero false-positive refactors in our canonical test corpus.

3) SDK integration hooks that allow the tool to open a draft PR in GitHub and include an automated migration report with token-cost/latency estimates for the change. The PR template must include rollback instructions and a link to telemetry gating docs.

4) Migration telemetry gating rules defined and implemented: canary cohort (1% users) health checks for 48h, automatic rollback criteria on error-rate delta > 2x baseline or quality regression > 5% for a tracked prompt set. Metrics and dashboards created in Console.
5) Internal runbook and support playbook written for Success and Support teams with common customer Q&A and escalation paths.
6) Developer documentation and sample repo demonstrating automated migration for Node, Python, and Java SDKs, with at least one successful customer pilot recorded (internal notes).

migration_timeline: Phase 0 (Jan-Feb 2025): Spec + prototype + internal dry-run; collect canonical corpora and edge-case examples.
Phase 1 (Mar 2025): Beta tool for Redwood SDK customers; opt-in automatic PRs for repos that have opted in; monitor via telemetry gating.
Phase 2 (Apr-May 2025): Expand to public CLI and community docs; lift opt-in to suggested migration but require customer approval for automated PRs.
Phase 3 (June 2025): Begin coordinated removal window for legacy endpoints for hosted API after confirmed pilot success and safety gates.
rollback_criteria: Error rate increase > 2x baseline for canary cohort over 1h window
Quality regression measured on benchmark prompt set > 5% (BLEU/ROUGE where applicable or model-specific score),
Unresolved customer-reported functional regressions in top 5 support cases within 24h
